task: Define stable cross-package generic nominal identities and ABI-v10 contracts from the pinned ABI-v9 baseline.
observation: The ABI-v9 interface emits `module_id <package>::<module>`, but source-free loading reduces it to the final module component before semantic composition, while semantic type equality and specialization still use canonical strings and parameter-type vectors. This made package-qualified nominal identity impossible to inherit safely and required ABI v10 to freeze one structured identity contract rather than extending the existing spellings.
impact: The G0 design must change module loading, Type IR, specialization keys, and ABI serialization together; an isolated nominal-type patch could conflate providers or give separate compiler subsystems different identities.

resolution.summary: The proposed Type IR and ABI-v10 contracts define package-qualified ModuleIdentity and SHA-256 type/specialization keys; implementation remains blocked on Team S and written L7 G0 acknowledgement.

tool_used: repository-local bootstrap, ABI documentation, and compiler source inspection
suggestion: Expose the exact module/package/type identity schema through agent capability discovery so ABI design and cross-package diagnosis do not require compiler-source archaeology.
